en.hubeali: From him, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from a man, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Al A’ala Bin Kamil who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘From the supplication what is befitting for its performer when he forgets it, that he should make up for it, is that he should be saying after the morning (Salat),

‘There is no god except Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Alone, there being no associates for him. For Him<sup>azwj</sup> is the Kingdom and for Him is the Praise. He<sup>azwj</sup> Causes to like and He<sup>azwj</sup> Causes to die, and He<sup>azwj</sup> is Living and will not be dying. In His Hand is the goodness, all of it, and He<sup>azwj</sup> is Able upon everything’, ten times.
And he should be saying, ‘I seek Refuge with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the Hearing, the Knowing’, ten times.
So if he forgets anything from that, it would be upon him to make up for it’.
en.sarwar: 33. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Isma’Il ibn Mehran from a man from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from al-‘Ala’ ibn Kamil
who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Of the prayers are such that if one forgets one should make up for it.

One should say after the morning prayer, “No one deserves to be worshipped except Allah, alone Who has no partner, to Him belongs the Kingdom and all praise, He gives life, causes death, causes death, gives life, He is living and does not die, in His hand is all good and He has power over all things,” ten times.
One should then say, ‘I seek protection with Allah, the Hearing, the Omniscient,’ ten times
and if one forgets any of this, he owes to make it up for them.’”
